_description: VG-SOURCE-CLASS cases (18.127): each case is one bundle for the fixture subject, judged against the baseline catalog and the Conduct overlay; expected is the named control's outcome, its failing event ids and the assess exit code, with nothing quarantined, the same in Python, TypeScript and Java. A control's min_source_class holds per assertion (SPEC HR-5, §6.4): a focus whose judged class is below the minimum reads insufficient_evidence, never conformant. CND-04 and CND-05 judge the acted-on instruction (evaluation.source_class_from actsOn), which counts as enforcement_point only when attested: held by graph IRI, every parent attested, any origin an enforcement-point read at trust_min trusted, and its own class enforcement_point or witnessed by an attested enforcement-point twin (same content_ref, refs.task, source_class and principal, every instruction above it of a trusted class) or by an enforcement-point PolicyDecision allow for the acting call and the instruction's principal (SPEC §7.7.5, §10.4, §6.2.3, Appendix F). probe-* are the audit probes A to J, each beside an attested twin that stays conformant; hostile-* each differ by one field from a hostile-base-attested-* case; unknown-class-* hold no events: CND-05's min_source_class in a copy of the Conduct overlay is set to the value given (or removed), and every engine must refuse the catalog at load with the key and exit given.

hostile-base-attested-policy-decision.why: base: an enforcement-point PolicyDecision allows the acting call for the instruction's principal

hostile-base-attested-policy-decision-ep.why: base: the acted-on instruction's parent is an enforcement-point user instruction

hostile-base-attested-twin.why: base: the agent's user instruction and an enforcement-point twin with the same content, task, class, principal

hostile-base-attested-twin-ep-parent.why: base: the twin's parent is an enforcement-point user instruction

hostile-base-attested-twin-trusted-origi.why: base: the twin's origin is an enforcement-point memory read at trust_min trusted

hostile-pd-other-request.why: the PolicyDecision's refs.request names another tool call

hostile-pd-self-report.why: the PolicyDecision is the agent's own record

hostile-pd-sr-parent.why: the acted-on instruction's parent is the agent's own record

hostile-twin-other-authorised-class.why: the twin declares operator where the agent says user

hostile-twin-other-subject.why: the twin is recorded under another subject

hostile-twin-sr-parent.why: the twin's parent is the agent's own record

hostile-twin-tool_output-parent.why: the twin's parent is an enforcement-point tool_output instruction

hostile-twin-untrusted-origin.why: the twin's origin is an enforcement-point memory read at trust_min untrusted

probe-a-attested-ingress-twin.why: twin of A: an enforcement-point ingress record of the same instruction (content, task, class, principal)

probe-a-attested-policy-decision.why: twin of A: an enforcement-point PolicyDecision allows the call for the instruction's principal

probe-a-self-report-user.why: A: the agent's own record says the instruction came from the user; one enforcement-point call acts on it

probe-b-all-self-report.why: B: instruction and call are both the agent's own records

probe-b-attested-enforcement-point.why: twin of B: instruction and call both recorded by enforcement points

probe-c-attested-ingress-agrees.why: twin of C: the ingress record of the same content says user too, for the same principal

probe-c-ingress-tool-output-relabelled.why: C: the ingress recorded tool_output; the agent's twin of the same content says user and the call acts on it

probe-d-attested-enforcement-point.why: twin of D: the instruction and the acting call recorded by enforcement points

probe-d-self-report-beside-unrelated-ep.why: D: acting call, decision and instruction all self_report, beside an unrelated enforcement-point call and read

probe-e1-attested-held.why: twin of E1: the instruction is held, recorded by the ingress

probe-e1-instruction-not-held.why: E1: a consequential call names an instruction the bundle does not hold

probe-e2-attested-graph-iri.why: twin of E2: the call names the instruction by its graph IRI

probe-e2-bare-id.why: E2: the call names the held enforcement-point instruction by its bare event id, not its graph IRI

probe-f-attested-enforcement-point.why: twin of F: the ingress recorded the memory_trusted instruction

probe-f-self-report-memory-trusted-no-or.why: F: the agent says the instruction came from trusted memory and names no read

probe-h-attested-instruction.why: twin of H: the call acts on an instruction the ingress recorded

probe-h-decision-no-instruction.why: H: a consequential decision acts on no instruction, and the enforcement-point call executing it names none

probe-i-attested-verified-delegation.why: twin of I: the instruction recorded by the ingress, the delegation verified

probe-i-unverified-delegation-no-princip.why: I: a consequential call under a delegation whose verification failed, acting on a self_report instruction with no principal

probe-j-cnd-04-attested-user.why: twin of J (CND-04): the ingress recorded the instruction as user

probe-j-cnd-04-no-source-class.why: J (CND-04): the acted-on instruction declares no source_class and is the agent's own record

probe-j-cnd-05-attested-user.why: twin of J (CND-05): the ingress recorded the instruction as user

probe-j-cnd-05-no-source-class.why: J (CND-05): the acted-on instruction declares no source_class and is the agent's own record

probe-j-rob-02-attested-user.why: twin of J (ROB-02): the ingress recorded the instruction as user

probe-j-rob-02-no-source-class.why: J (ROB-02): the acted-on instruction declares no source_class and is the agent's own record
